---
title: "metest"
subtitle: "Tests and contrasts of marginal effects"
---

`metest` tests linear and nonlinear combinations of the rows of the table
produced by [`mecompare`](../mecompare/index.html),
[`meinequality`](../meinequality/index.html), or
[`totalme`](../totalme/index.html) -- or of any results posted by
`margins, post`. Rows are referred to by the number in the `#` column of the
table, so a difference between two effects is `metest 2 - 1`, a ratio is
`metest 2 / 1`, and a test that several effects are equal is
`metest 1 = 2 = 3`.

## Installation

```stata
net install metest, from("https://tdmize.github.io/data/metest") replace
```

<!-- CHECK: install location. -->

## Basic use

```{.stata-run}
. sysuse nlsw88, clear
(NLSW, 1988 extract)

. drop if missing(union)
(368 observations deleted)

. 
. quietly logit union i.collgrad i.south i.smsa c.age c.wage, vce(robust)

. estimates store m

. 
. mecompare i.collgrad i.south i.smsa, models(m)


Predicting: Pr(union)

Marginal effects (N_m=1878)

                                 |  ME #   Estimate  Robust SE      P>|z|
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
collgrad                         |                                       
         College  - Not coll     |                                       
                               m |     1      0.056      0.025      0.026
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
south                            |                                       
            South - Not sout     |                                       
                               m |     2     -0.114      0.020      0.000
---------------------------------+---------------------------------------
smsa                             |                                       
             SMSA - Not SMSA     |                                       
                               m |     3      0.031      0.022      0.161

```

Is the college gap in union membership the same size as the regional gap? And
is the college gap larger than the city/non-city gap?

```{.stata-run}
. metest 1 - 2

                                 |  estimate         se     pvalue 
---------------------------------+--------------------------------
                collgrad - south |     0.170      0.034      0.000 

. metest 1 - 3

                                 |  estimate         se     pvalue 
---------------------------------+--------------------------------
                 collgrad - smsa |     0.025      0.034      0.465 

```
